o: Each query brings a window to the top of the stack. Final order: process queries from last to first — the last queried window ends on top, then earlier distinct queried windows, then all never-queried windows in their original relative order. Example 1: queries [3,3,2] reversed-distinct = [2,3], unqueried = [1] → [2,3,1]. ✓
k: Work backwards through queries, taking each window the first time you see it (dedupe).
Append windows never mentioned in queries, preserving original order.

a.i: The final stack top-down is exactly the sequence of last-to-first distinct queried windows followed by untouched windows — no per-query simulation needed.
s: Build set Q of queried ids.
Scan queries right-to-left, collecting unseen ids.
Append windows not in Q in original order.

a.n: Approach 2: Direct Simulation with Order Statistic / Linked Structure
a.i: Simulate each query by moving the window to front using a doubly linked list of positions — O(1) per move after O(n) setup, useful if queries had to be answered interleaved with other operations.
s: Build doubly linked list in initial order with node pointers.
For each query: unlink node, relink at head.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def finalState(self, windows: List[int], queries: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        nxt = list(range(1, len(windows) + 2))
        prv = list(range(-1, len(windows)))
        head = 0
        for q in queries:
            node = q - 1
            if node == head: continue
            prv[nxt[node]] = prv[node]
            nxt[prv[node]] = nxt[node]
            prv[node] = -1
            nxt[node] = head
            prv[head] = node
            head = node
        res, cur = [], head
        while cur < len(windows):
            res.append(windows[cur]); cur = nxt[cur]
        return res

w: The reverse-dedup trick is the elegant one-liner interviewers love; the linked list generalizes to online settings. Pitfall: duplicates in queries must collapse to a single occurrence. Follow-up: interleave queries with 'close window' operations — then the linked list wins.
